name: MK-677
lead: MK-677, also known as ibutamoren (developmental codes MK-0677, L-163,191 and, in more recent development, LUM-201), is an orally active, non-peptide drug that mimics the hormone ghrelin. By activating the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) in the pituitary and hypothalamus, it raises growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels and also raises cortisol and appetite.[1][2][17] It was developed by Merck in the 1990s and has never been approved for any indication; it remains an investigational compound.[1][2]

Human trials in older adults, obese men, dieting volunteers and patients recovering from hip fracture have shown that it increases GH and IGF-1 and increases fat-free mass, while studies for functional benefit, Alzheimer's disease and frailty have not shown clear clinical gains, and a heart-failure safety signal was reported in a hip-fracture trial.[6][8][12][2] Reported adverse effects include increased appetite, fluid retention, lethargy and reduced insulin sensitivity.[12][4]

MK-677 is sold online as a research chemical, discussed on bodybuilding and physique forums as an oral alternative to injectable growth hormone or peptides, and prohibited in sport.[1][29] No trial has tested it for cosmetic or aesthetic outcomes in healthy people.

paras: Ibutamoren is a selective agonist of the ghrelin receptor and mimics the GH-stimulating action of the gut hormone ghrelin. It belongs to the non-peptide (spiroindoline) mimetics of the earlier peptide secretagogue family, and unlike peptides it is orally active.[1][18] Pharmacological studies show it acts as a simple agonist at the receptor, activating signalling pathways with high potency, and structural work has described how it binds the human ghrelin receptor.[16][17]

Unlike injected growth hormone, secretagogues work through the pituitary's own release machinery, and reviews describe GH release as pulsatile and subject to negative feedback, though the acute effect partially desensitizes while prolonged intermittent oral administration still raises IGF-1.[4][18] Wikipedia reports that ibutamoren raises GH, IGF-1 and cortisol.[1]
A set of human trials published between 1996 and 2011 examined MK-677 in healthy volunteers, older adults and patient groups.

Healthy older adults: A 1996 randomized, double-blind trial in 32 healthy people aged 64 to 81 reported that daily oral MK-677 stimulated the GH-IGF-1 axis.[13] A 2008 randomized trial in healthy older adults tested whether the oral ghrelin mimetic could restore GH secretion toward young-adult levels, preserve fat-free mass and improve clinical outcomes; it reported increased fat-free mass and IGF-1 alongside increased appetite, fluid retention and reduced insulin sensitivity, without functional improvement.[12][4]

Dieting volunteers and obesity: In a double-blind crossover study, MK-677 reversed diet-induced protein catabolism in healthy volunteers during calorie restriction.[5] A two-month study in obese subjects reported increased GH secretion, fat-free mass and energy expenditure.[14]

Hip fracture and frailty: A phase IIb multicentre trial in 123 elderly hip-fracture patients tested 25 mg per day against placebo for functional recovery and IGF-1 levels.[6] A trial in post-hip-fracture sarcopenia was terminated, and one report describes a congestive heart failure signal in a limited number of patients.[2][6]

Bone: Studies in healthy and functionally impaired older adults found that oral MK-677 increased markers of bone turnover, and a trial combined it with alendronate in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.[9][15]
Sleep: Prolonged oral treatment improved sleep quality in men in a controlled study.[10]
Alzheimer's disease: A randomized trial found that MK-677 had no clinical effect on disease progression, despite raising IGF-1.[8][2]

Children and newer work: A trial in children with growth hormone deficiency examined its effect on the GH-IGF-1 axis.[7] A recent review notes preliminary data on an oral secretagogue in children with partial GH deficiency, and Phase 3 trials of LUM-201 in pediatric growth hormone deficiency are registered.[21][23] A small trial in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease has been completed and fibromyalgia and chronic kidney disease studies have been registered.[20][22]

No trial has evaluated MK-677 for facial or cosmetic outcomes in healthy people. A 2018 review concluded that few long-term, rigorously controlled studies have examined the efficacy and safety of growth hormone secretagogues.[4]

Effects reported in trials and reviews include increased appetite, fluid retention, lethargy, reduced insulin sensitivity and elevated cortisol, and the reviews flag the unknown long-term consequences of sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation.[4][2] One hip-fracture study was reported to carry a congestive heart failure signal.[2] A 2025 case report described hepatotoxicity attributed to MK-677.[11] Merck stopped broader development in the late 1990s and early 2000s after mixed efficacy results, according to one summary, and there are no authoritative long-term safety data in healthy people.[2]

MK-677 originated in Merck's work in the 1990s on orally active non-peptide growth hormone secretagogues.[2][18] Merck-sponsored trials in the late 1990s and 2000s tested it for diet-induced catabolism, age-related decline, hip fracture recovery and Alzheimer's disease, and development stalled after limited clinical benefit.[5][6][8][2] The compound later passed to Lumos Pharma under the code LUM-201, which is in Phase 3 development for pediatric growth hormone deficiency, and Wikipedia notes that topline data from Phase 2 trials met their primary and secondary endpoints.[1][2][21]

Ibutamoren is an investigational new drug in the United States and is not approved for marketing for human consumption, although it has been used experimentally by some in the bodybuilding community; its use is banned in most sports.[1]

subs.h: Use in physique and looksmaxxing communities
paras: On T Nation, MK-677 is discussed by people who describe using it for appetite, recovery, joint comfort and as an oral GH booster, often alongside testosterone or SARMs; one thread asks about adding it and the SARM ostarine to a 'blast and cruise' steroid regimen.[24][25] Users report mixed experiences: one person on clinic-prescribed ibutamoren with low IGF-1 reported noticing no difference after two months, another says it made them feel 'like I was on a drug' with hunger and lethargy, and another reports that the appetite increase led them to eat out of control.[24][26][27] A commenter on joint comfort writes that MK-677 seemed to have their joints feeling better than in a long time.[28]

timeline.event: Randomized trial in healthy elderly shows stimulation of the GH-IGF-1 axis.[13]
Trials report reversal of diet-induced catabolism and increased fat-free mass in obese subjects.[5][14]
Randomized trial in healthy older adults and a randomized Alzheimer's disease trial are published.[12][8]
Case report of hepatotoxicity associated with MK-677; Phase 3 trials of LUM-201 begin for pediatric deficiency.[11][21]

lore.intro: MK-677 is discussed on T Nation as a simple oral way to raise GH and IGF-1, valued for appetite and recovery effects, and frequently contrasted with injectable HGH and peptides.[24][28][29]

claims.claim: MK-677 raises GH/IGF-1 and improves recovery, joints and body composition
claims.believers: Forum members say it helped joint comfort and recovery, and some are prescribed it by clinics after low IGF-1 labs.[24][28]
claims.experts: Trials confirm increased GH, IGF-1 and fat-free mass in older adults and obese men, but not clear functional gains, and effects on joints have not been established.[12][14][6]

claims.claim: It is a good bulking aid because it makes you ravenous
claims.believers: Posters describe using it to increase appetite, with one stopping because they 'went out of control' eating and another reporting hunger and lethargy.[26][27]
claims.experts: Increased appetite is a documented effect of ghrelin-receptor agonists in trials and reviews.[12][4]

claims.claim: MK-677 can be stacked with testosterone or SARMs to protect muscle on a cycle
claims.believers: A thread asks about adding ibutamoren and ostarine to a blast-and-cruise testosterone cycle to limit muscle loss.[25]
claims.experts: No published trial has tested MK-677 alongside androgens; reviews state that data on clinical efficacy of secretagogues in hypogonadal men are lacking.[3]

claims.believers: It is often sold and discussed in the same marketplace as SARMs, including on Amazon-style listings mentioned in forums.[29]
claims.experts: Pharmacologically it is a ghrelin receptor agonist and growth hormone secretagogue, not a selective androgen receptor modulator.[1]

claims.claim: MK-677 is safe for long-term use because it works through the body's own feedback
claims.believers: Forum users frame it as a milder alternative to HGH.[28]
claims.experts: Reviews say long-term effects of sustained IGF-1 elevation are unknown; trials reported insulin-sensitivity changes, edema and a heart-failure signal in a frail hip-fracture population, and a hepatotoxicity case report exists.[4][2][6][11]
